title: Test whether a generator matches the LSA score distribution and its boundary tail on consecutive pages
statement: I followed up the raw-frequency comparison in P-G-002 with the window method in Layfield and Davis (2026), https://dhq.digitalhumanities.org/vol/20/1/000857/000857.html. I froze model tables, vocabulary, IDF and projection on public training pages, then evaluated distinct public practice pages in binding order. On 274 ZL windows the manuscript's 5th, 25th, 50th, 75th and 95th percentiles were 0.504, 0.661, 0.730, 0.820 and 0.877; on 271 Takahashi windows they were 0.516, 0.666, 0.731, 0.804 and 0.867. Three draws from a single repository line-chain table gave empirical CDF distances of 0.347–0.427 in ZL and 0.306–0.391 in Takahashi. The same chain pooled by section and Currier label improved those ranges to 0.197–0.215 and 0.196–0.255. Yet its median scores were 0.799–0.803 and 0.783–0.798, and its low tail contained more cross-label boundaries than the manuscript: 4–5 of the lowest 13 windows in ZL and 4–6 in Takahashi versus 3 in both manuscript transcriptions. A chain using 20 nearby public training pages per fixed 12-page positional bin gave CDF distances of 0.350–0.376 and 0.266–0.395 and 2 of 13 low windows at transitions in both transcriptions. The repository self-citation procedure had distances of 0.719–0.777 and 0.683–0.823, with up to 5 windows lacking a nonzero projected comparison. All distances used matching valid windows. The standard practice split concatenates retained pages across omissions. In a second public split, retaining only windows that crossed no missing page, the grouped chain still enriched transitions in the low tail but now had larger CDF distances than the global chain in both transcriptions. That split exposed only 4 and 3 eligible cross-label boundaries. A boundary-conditioned generator can put low scores near reference transitions, while matching the overall distribution remains open and the ordering of the two chains depends on the sampling design.
check: Use certain P, C and R tokens, grouped by page and unit. For target size 20 or 40, discard groups shorter than half the target and divide the rest into nearest-integer numbers of blocks with lengths differing by at most one. Fit separate rank-75 TF-IDF SVD spaces from the size-40 training documents of each stream, using raw count times log(document count / document frequency), and project practice documents with the frozen weighted term basis. Compare cosine scores for adjacent nonoverlapping windows of ten size-20 documents, advancing one document at a time. Record five quantiles, empirical CDF distance, undefined cosine count, cross-label median versus other page breaks, and the count of section or Currier transitions in the bottom floor(0.05 N) scores, breaking ties in window order. Match each synthetic stream to the practice line and page lengths. For each generator use training seeds 11, 22, 33 and practice seeds 20011, 20022, 20033. The grouped model fits the existing order-four line chain by section and Currier label, backs off to section and then global if fewer than 400 certain tokens are available, and offsets seeds by 1009 times the target group's first-appearance index. The drifting model uses page order divided into 12-page bins, fits on the 20 training pages nearest each bin center and offsets seeds by 1009 times the bin index. Repeat on contiguous public reserves using seeds 11 and 22, withhold pages for which floor(page order / 8) modulo 4 equals 1 from the public training partition, and reject any window spanning an omitted page. Confirm the tail comparison on a reserve with substantially more eligible transitions before assigning statistical weight to it.
